summary: Lavina Mountain, BC: tower burned in the 2024 Argenta Creek wildfire, leaving a concrete base; volunteers began a rebuild in July 2026 and the site is not described as open.

facts.design: Two-story flat-cab tower (NHLR); the first lookout on the site was built in 1937
facts.status_note: Burned in the Argenta Creek wildfire in summer 2024; the walls were later demolished, the concrete base remains, and a rebuild began in July 2026
facts.agency: British Columbia Forest Service (per NHLR); Recreation Sites and Trails of British Columbia (RSTBC) holds the site maintenance contract (per 4WDABC)

access.note: Trail closed in September 2024; the association said it needed permission from RSTBC to go up. A local contractor, Sunshine Logging LTD., cleared the road before the July 2025 event (per 4WDABC). The 2026 update does not describe public access.

visit.trail_note: Four-wheel-drive trail to the site; the tower is gone, so there is no structure to climb

events.note: First lookout on the site (NHLR description)
Two-story flat-cab tower replaced the first lookout; NHLR 'Built' field gives 1959
4WDABC says the tower has stood since 1974; this conflicts with the NHLR's 1959 date
Became home to a West Kootenay Amateur Radio Club repeater
Lost to the Argenta Creek wildfire in summer 2024; only the concrete block base appeared to remain (4WDABC, September 2024)
Trail to Lavina described as closed in a September 2024 update
Walls demolished by excavator during a volunteer maintenance event; concrete slab kept (4WDABC update dated July 29, 2025)
First rebuild work event, late July 2026: debris removal, rebar fixed to the old foundation with epoxy, forms built for a future concrete pour. Rebuild not complete.

corrections.why: NHLR says the tower burned in summer 2024 and lists it as removed in 2024; 4WDABC says only the concrete base appeared to remain after the Argenta Creek wildfire
The loss was a wildfire, not a removal; the 2025 demolition removed only the walls and the slab was kept

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1937 for the first lookout and 1959 for the flat-cab tower; 4WDABC says the tower has stood since 1974. The sources disagree and no source reconciles them. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. The 4WDABC page is a volunteer association's own account, dated by update headings (Sept 28 2024, July 29 2025, July 30 2026); the 2025 demolition date is inferred from the July 29, 2025 update. Build-date conflict (1959 NHLR vs 1974 4WDABC) is unresolved. The brief's 'standing' status and '2024 removed' event were wrong. Not searched: BC Wildfire Service, RSTBC or BC Forest Service records for the site; Sites and Trails BC page did not load. Facebook and AdventureTaco search hits were not read. No photos added.
